one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q4 2026 results come in late January 2027 (Q4 2025 was reported 2026-01-22, src 5). Inside the window: possible announcement of the 'couple' of customers the CEO expects within two quarters of the call (src 6), a mild positive; the December FOMC as a sector-wide macro print; no Intel filing or company fact on Nov 20-23. The stock jumped 16.3% on 11-23 (51.28 to 59.66, src 16) in a sector rebound on NVIDIA's CEO news, after a ~58% fall from the June peak; reversal and momentum effects roughly offset after such a move. So the ladder stays a symmetric lognormal at $59.66 with monthly sigma = 86% / 3.5 = 24.6%, no drift (unchanged from round 1: nothing the supervisor found falls inside the window).

inputs_detail.derivation: Q4 FY2026 6,300 = Q3 8,097 x 0.78 (CFO: CCPG down 'greater than 20%' sequentially, src 17). FY2027 26,400 (-15% on FY2026 31,001): industry PC units 2027 between IDC -3.1% for all personal computing devices (src 20) and the CFO's -10% planning view (src 17), about -5% to -6%; on top of that Intel's FY2026 ran on an H1 sell-in pull-in (Q1-Q3 averaged 8,234 a quarter vs the 6,300 Q4 exit) and Intel is moving Oregon wafers from client to Intel 3 Xeon (CEO, src 17), partly offset by memory-driven price increases (IDC, src 20). Quarters are built off the 6,300 exit, not a past seasonal shape: Q1 6,100 (CFO: H1 2027 the more challenging half, src 17), Q2 6,300, then H2 6,900 / 7,100 as substrate and Intel 3 capacity eases (src 17). FY2028 28,700 (+9%): IDC +2.0% devices 2028 (src 20) plus a full year at the H2 2027 run-rate and the 14-week Q1 FY2028 (7,200). Other evidence-based builds: CFO -10% units applied to the FY2026 base (~$28B, no pull-in reversal); consensus total revenue (src 9) implies ~$27-28B; Omdia -7% and Counterpoint ~flat for 2027 (supervisor review) bracket the unit view.

inputs_detail.derivation: Supply build (supervisor asked for a capacity path into 2028). Q4 FY2026 8,350 = Q3 7,318 x 1.14 (CFO: 'mid-teens percent sequentially', src 17), after the ~$300M Fab 28 hit that is almost all 10nm server (CFO, src 17). FY2027 36,700 (+36%): H1 capped (CFO: 'still constrained on Intel 3'; market share 'a function of supply', src 17): Q1 8,200 (Fab 28 recovery), Q2 8,700. H2 is where capacity lands: +40% substrate capacity, 'a lot of that' in the back half (CFO), and Oregon Intel 3 for Xeon in production in H2 2027 (CEO, src 17): Q3 9,500, Q4 10,300, i.e. the Q4 exit is +18% on Q2, less than the +40% substrate add because wafers (Intel 3) and materials (Unimicron: 20% substrate material gap in 2027, src 18) still bind. FY2028 42,000 (+14%): supply roughly flat at the Q4 2027 exit rate (10,300 a quarter) with the 14-week Q1 (10,800) and no further large wafer or substrate step dated before end-2028 (equipment lead times up to 30 months, src 18); the CFO expects the industry constrained 'into 2028' (src 17), so supply rather than demand caps volume, while Arm (~30% of server CPUs in 2027) and AMD (~27% in 2026, rising) take the rest of a market growing >40% in 2027 (TrendForce, src 19). Other evidence-based builds: TrendForce units x an Intel share of ~40% (100 - Arm 30 - AMD ~30, low-confidence derivation) gives Intel units ~+6% in 2027 (1.40 x 40/53) and ~$31-33B with ~10% price; capacity at the full +40% substrate add from Q4 2027 would give ~$46-48B in 2028 (near the supervisor's booked $47.9B).
inputs_detail.variant_view: Share loss bites as soon as supply loosens (FY2028 ~$38B): research target (12m) about -$6; full +40% substrate add converts to units (FY2028 ~$47B): about +$6.

FY2028 fades to 36-38%: Arm ~30% and AMD rising (src 19) compete for incremental hyperscaler sockets as supply loosens, and Diamond Rapids ramps on a new node (18A-P) with start-up costs. downside.story: P10: PC units fall ~20% in 2027 (memory prices stay at 5x, OEMs keep cutting), CCPG ~$23B at ~18% margin; server supply relief arrives just as AMD/Arm price aggressively so DCAI misses by 15% at ~36% margins; foundry losses widen with 14A start-up and no external anchor customer; 2027 capex ~$28B with negative FCF and the market pays ~24x for trough-ish EPS.

base.story: Q4 lands inside the guide; CCPG falls 15% in 2027 (~$26.4B) and recovers 9% in 2028 at 22-25% margins; DCAI is supply-capped in H1 2027, steps up in H2 as the +40% substrate add and Oregon Intel 3 wafers land (~$36.7B), then runs flat at that exit rate in 2028 (~$42.0B) at a fading 37% margin as Arm and AMD take the incremental sockets; foundry losses narrow from ~$7.8B to $6.0B; FY2027 EPS ~$1.36 (consensus $1.31), FY2028 ~$1.89; 5.44B shares; capex ~$26B with FCF ~-$4B in 2027; the multiple shrinks from 46.5x toward 40.5x.

upside.story: P90: memory prices roll over in H1 2027 and the PC decline is ~-5%; substrates and wafers loosen early so DCAI ships ~$42B in 2027 with 10% price held; a named 14A anchor customer and the two packaging customers cut the foundry loss by 40% and re-rate the stock toward its June peak multiple.

reasoning: Round 2 rebuild on the supervisor's findings. Shares: restated to the CFO's 5.44B Q4 fully diluted count (transcript, src 17) with 0% a year, since GAAP EBIT already expenses SBC (round 1 counted SBC twice). Peers re-struck at 11-23 closes (src 16) on Zacks consensus opened 11-24 (src 15): median 23.3x (was 22.4x on 10-30 prices), own 46.5x, exit 40.5x by the k=0.8 rule. DCAI rebuilt from capacity: H1 2027 capped (CFO: constrained on Intel 3; share a function of supply), H2 steps up with the +40% substrate add and Oregon Intel 3 wafers (CFO/CEO), and FY2028 runs flat at the Q4 2027 exit plus the 14th week because further wafer/substrate steps need up to 30-month tool lead times (Unimicron, src 18) and Arm/AMD take the rest of a market TrendForce sees >40% larger in 2027 (src 19); FY2028 DCAI $42.0B (round 1 $41.8B) with margin fading to 37%. CCPG re-based on IDC's 10-30 forecast (-3.1% devices 2027, +2.0% 2028) against the CFO's -10% plan: $26.4B / $28.7B. NCI raised to the CFO's ~$1.1B a year. Net: FY2027 EPS ~$1.36 (consensus $1.31), FY2028 ~$1.89; research target (12m) $68.41 (round 1 $69.29). Scenario deltas kept (P10 $29.2, P90 $123.5): an 86%-vol name needs wide tails. Research was limited to ~8 follow-ups.

Forecast: CFO on the Q3 call (src 6): CCPG down >20% q/q in Q4, PC unit TAM -12% in 2026 (H2 down >20%) and about -10% in 2027 with the sharpest declines in H1; IDC 3Q26 units -20.1% y/y, -9.1% q/q, prices elevated (src 13). Revision: CFO and CEO on the call as read in the full transcript (src 17); IDC forecast page 2026-10-30 (src 20).
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY2026 6,300 = Q3 8,097 x 0.78 (CFO: CCPG down 'greater than 20%' sequentially, src 17). FY2027 26,400 (-15% on FY2026 31,001): industry PC units 2027 between IDC -3.1% for all personal computing devices (src 20) and the CFO's -10% planning view (src 17), about -5% to -6%; on top of that Intel's FY2026 ran on an H1 sell-in pull-in (Q1-Q3 averaged 8,234 a quarter vs the 6,300 Q4 exit) and Intel is moving Oregon wafers from client to Intel 3 Xeon (CEO, src 17), partly offset by memory-driven price increases (IDC, src 20). Quarters are built off the 6,300 exit, not a past seasonal shape: Q1 6,100 (CFO: H1 2027 the more challenging half, src 17), Q2 6,300, then H2 6,900 / 7,100 as substrate and Intel 3 capacity eases (src 17). FY2028 28,700 (+9%): IDC +2.0% devices 2028 (src 20) plus a full year at the H2 2027 run-rate and the 14-week Q1 FY2028 (7,200). Other evidence-based builds: CFO -10% units applied to the FY2026 base (~$28B, no pull-in reversal); consensus total revenue (src 9) implies ~$27-28B; Omdia -7% and Counterpoint ~flat for 2027 (supervisor review) bracket the unit view.
drivers.why: PC CPUs are ~45% of FY2026 revenue; the PC unit cycle (memory-price driven) is the single largest swing in the Q4-2027 path, so the segment line carries the PC unit view directly.
drivers.variant: Consensus-like path (CCPG ~$28.5B in FY2027): FY2028 EPS ~+$0.08, research target (12m) about +$3.

drivers.label: CCPG operating margin (segment basis)
drivers.source: Actuals: segment operating income / revenue from src 5, 4, 3, 2 (FY2025 28.9%; Q1-Q3 2026 32.6% / 26.4% / 28.2%). CFO: Q4 gross margin falls on lower revenue against the fixed cost base and 18A underloading (src 6); KeyBanc: 18A costs down ~40% since Q1 (src 11).
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY2026 18%: a ~$1.75B revenue drop at a ~60% decremental (CFO fall-through 40-60%, src 6) takes segment profit from $2,285M to ~$1,150M. FY2027 19% rising to 24% as 18A Panther Lake costs fall (src 11) and volumes recover in H2; FY2028 25%, still below the FY2025 28.9% because volumes stay ~14% below FY2025. Alternative anchors: FY2025 28.9% (reported history, src 5) and the 2026 YTD 28.9%.
drivers.why: Fixed-cost absorption on falling PC volumes is the margin swing the playbook asks to model.
drivers.variant: Back to 28% by FY2028 (FY2025 level): FY2028 EBIT +$0.8B, research target (12m) about +$4.

drivers.label: Data Center & AI revenue (Xeon server CPUs), $M per quarter
drivers.source: Actuals: src 5, 4, 3, 2 (Q3 2026 $7,318M, +78% y/y). CFO (src 6): DCAI to grow mid-teens % sequentially in Q4; demand meaningfully exceeds supply; H1 2027 tighter on wafers and substrates; industry server CPU units +30% in 2026 and 2027; share a function of supply. KeyBanc: ~10% server CPU price hikes (src 12). CEO: server CPU TAM $40B to >$200B over 5 years (src 6).
drivers.derivation: Supply build (supervisor asked for a capacity path into 2028). Q4 FY2026 8,350 = Q3 7,318 x 1.14 (CFO: 'mid-teens percent sequentially', src 17), after the ~$300M Fab 28 hit that is almost all 10nm server (CFO, src 17). FY2027 36,700 (+36%): H1 capped (CFO: 'still constrained on Intel 3'; market share 'a function of supply', src 17): Q1 8,200 (Fab 28 recovery), Q2 8,700. H2 is where capacity lands: +40% substrate capacity, 'a lot of that' in the back half (CFO), and Oregon Intel 3 for Xeon in production in H2 2027 (CEO, src 17): Q3 9,500, Q4 10,300, i.e. the Q4 exit is +18% on Q2, less than the +40% substrate add because wafers (Intel 3) and materials (Unimicron: 20% substrate material gap in 2027, src 18) still bind. FY2028 42,000 (+14%): supply roughly flat at the Q4 2027 exit rate (10,300 a quarter) with the 14-week Q1 (10,800) and no further large wafer or substrate step dated before end-2028 (equipment lead times up to 30 months, src 18); the CFO expects the industry constrained 'into 2028' (src 17), so supply rather than demand caps volume, while Arm (~30% of server CPUs in 2027) and AMD (~27% in 2026, rising) take the rest of a market growing >40% in 2027 (TrendForce, src 19). Other evidence-based builds: TrendForce units x an Intel share of ~40% (100 - Arm 30 - AMD ~30, low-confidence derivation) gives Intel units ~+6% in 2027 (1.40 x 40/53) and ~$31-33B with ~10% price; capacity at the full +40% substrate add from Q4 2027 would give ~$46-48B in 2028 (near the supervisor's booked $47.9B).
drivers.why: Supply-capped server CPU revenue: the disclosed segment line is the binding constraint (wafers, substrates), more informative than the unit TAM that exceeds what Intel can ship.
drivers.variant: Share loss bites as soon as supply loosens (FY2028 ~$38B): research target (12m) about -$6; full +40% substrate add converts to units (FY2028 ~$47B): about +$6.

drivers.label: DCAI operating margin (segment basis)
drivers.source: Actuals: src 5, 4, 3, 2 (FY2025 20.2%; Q1-Q3 2026 30.5% / 39.5% / 41.5%). CFO: Israel fab accident costs ~200bp of Q4 gross margin, mostly 10nm server (src 6).
drivers.derivation: Q2-Q3 2026 39.5% / 41.5% (src 3, 2) on scarcity pricing. Q4 2026 38% (Fab 28 hit on 10nm server, CFO src 17). 2027 39-41%: price held while the industry stays supply-constrained (CFO src 17; KeyBanc ~10% server CPU price rises, src 12) and Intel 3 cost down ~15% (src 11). FY2028 fades to 36-38%: Arm ~30% and AMD rising (src 19) compete for incremental hyperscaler sockets as supply loosens, and Diamond Rapids ramps on a new node (18A-P) with start-up costs. Other builds: the supervisor's booked ~39% (40% fall-through) and the forecaster median ~35%; Q1 2026 30.5% is the price-war floor.
drivers.why: Server pricing power vs share loss is the playbook's key debate for this segment.
drivers.variant: Margin back to 30% (Q1 2026 level) in a 2028 price war: FY2028 EBIT -$3.0B, research target (12m) about -$20; held at 40%: about +$7.

drivers.label: Intel Foundry + All Other + intersegment eliminations operating income (foundry losses net), $M per quarter
drivers.source: Actuals: segment table, src 5, 4, 3, 2 (FY2025 -9,435; Q1-Q3 2026 -2,114 / -1,605 / -1,744). CFO: Intel 3 profitable next year, considerable work ahead for a sustainably profitable foundry, 18A underloading headwind in Q4, 14A to begin production in 2028 (src 6). CEO: packaging customers to announce in the next two quarters (src 6).
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY2026 -2,300 (18A underloading, Israel outage, src 6). FY2027 -7,400 (-2,000 to -1,700): Intel 3 turns profitable and 18A costs fall (src 6, 11) against higher depreciation from capex up strongly (src 6) and 14A start-up. FY2028 -6,000: 14A production start (src 6) adds start-up cost while 18A matures; no external 14A wafer revenue assumed. Alternatives: management's earlier breakeven-by-end-2027 ambition (not restated on the Q3 call, src 6) would cut the FY2028 loss to ~0 (+$1.0/share EPS); the FY2025 run-rate of -9.4B (src 5).
drivers.why: Foundry losses are ~$1/share of after-tax earnings: the largest single lever on the horizon EPS.
drivers.variant: Breakeven by end-2027 as once targeted: FY2028 EPS +$0.98, research target (12m) about +$35 on the P/E leg.

Q1 FY2026.source: Q1 2026 release segment table (src 4); interest split of the YTD (F92 908 less Q3 324) evenly over Q1-Q2

Q3 FY2026.source: Q3 2026 release segment table (src 2); interest F93 324; other_income = interest income F97 461 less NCI income 200 (src 1)

quarters.note: GAAP basis: segment operating income per Intel's segment table; Foundry, All Other and eliminations = Intel Foundry + All Other + intersegment eliminations (revenue and operating income), i.e. external foundry, Mobileye/IMS and the elimination of inter-segment wafer sales. corporate_ebit = Corporate Unallocated (SBC, amortization, restructuring and other), constant -1,000 a quarter in forecasts (Q3 2026 -1,058, Q2 -1,416, FY2025 ex Q2 one-off ~-900/q, src 2, 3, 5). other_income = interest income less net income attributable to NCI (Q3 2026 NCI income $200M, src 1), so the P/E leg EPS is attributable to Intel.

quarters.note: Intel fiscal years end on the last Saturday of December. Ends through Q3 FY2026 from the filings (src 1, 2, 5); later ends by that calendar. FY2028 is a 53-week year (2027-12-25 to 2028-12-30); the extra week is placed in Q1 FY2028 as Intel did in 2022 (14-week Q1). actual = 4 + 3 (Q1-Q3 FY2026 in filed 10-Qs).

custom.name: Mid-cycle normalised EPS x peer P/E
custom.explanation: Playbook cross-check: mid-cycle EPS $2.19 x 23.3x peer median = $51.0. Mid-cycle EBIT $14.6B = CCPG $29B x 27% ($7.8B; FY2025 28.9%, Q1-Q3 2026 28.9%) + DCAI $40B x 37% ($14.8B; between the 2026 scarcity ~40% and a competitive ~33%) - foundry/other $4.0B (half way from FY2026 ~-$7.8B to breakeven) - corporate $4.0B = $14.6B; less below-the-line -$1.1B (interest income ~$1.36B on ~$40B cash at 3.4% less interest expense ~$1.36B less NCI $1.1B, CFO src 17) = $13.5B pretax x (1 - 12%) = $11.9B / 5.44B shares (CFO src 17) = $2.19. Not driver-linked.

downside.story: P10: PC units fall ~20% in 2027 (memory prices stay at 5x, OEMs keep cutting), CCPG ~$23B at ~18% margin; server supply relief arrives just as AMD/Arm price aggressively so DCAI misses by 15% at ~36% margins; foundry losses widen with 14A start-up and no external anchor customer; 2027 capex ~$28B with negative FCF and the market pays ~24x for trough-ish EPS.

upside.story: P90: memory prices roll over in H1 2027 and the PC decline is ~-5%; substrates and wafers loosen early so DCAI ships ~$42B in 2027 with 10% price held; a named 14A anchor customer and the two packaging customers cut the foundry loss by 40% and re-rate the stock toward its June peak multiple.

fit.segment: client + server x86 CPUs (CCPG + DCAI), FY2028
fit.why: the only other x86 CPU vendor; same PC and server CPU end markets
Snapdragon X PC SoCs and edge silicon; same PC OEMs, but handsets dominate QCOM
data-center compute incl. Grace Arm CPUs; same hyperscaler budgets
custom data-center silicon competing for the same server budgets
custom data-center silicon (including Arm CPUs for hyperscalers)

comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 5 peers: the run's peer table holds these five x86/data-center/client silicon names; TXN and ADI (analog) are excluded, TSM (Taiwan, foundry-only) and Samsung (Korea discount) are left out under the country rule, GlobalFoundries is a trailing-node pure-play foundry with no CPU business. No more genuine comparables to an integrated CPU designer-manufacturer exist.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 40.5x vs 23.3x median: the shrink rule keeps 80% of today's log gap (own 46.5x on calendar-NTM Zacks EPS $1.282, SBC expensed like the peers).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The premium is what the WRDS shrink rule keeps, not an outperformance call. It rests on depressed FY2027 earnings (foundry losses, PC trough) that the market capitalises above the run-rate, and on Intel being the only US leading-edge foundry (14A production targeted for 2028). The mid-cycle leg at the 23.3x peer median holds the blend back.

guidance_check.why: Slightly above the point guide on revenue just above the midpoint and the usual small beat, but well below the record-adjusted 40.7% because 18A underloading and the 200bp Israel hit are dated costs (src 6).

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly GAAP segment build (CCPG, DCAI, Foundry+All Other+eliminations; corporate unallocated as a constant).
